INTRO.text: Welcome to the Webapp Builder demo. This AI-powered tool transforms natural language descriptions into complete, runnable web applications with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Let's walk through the entire workflow.

HUB_OVERVIEW.text: This is the Cognotik App Hub, where all available applications are listed. Let's launch the Webapp Builder.

LOGIN_PROMPT.text: We need to log in first. Let me enter the credentials.

LOGIN_SUCCESS.text: Logged in successfully. Now we can see the App Hub with all available tools.

APP_OPENED.text: The Webapp Builder is now open. You can see the main interface with tabs for Idea, Pipeline, Update, Results, Git, and Usage tracking.

IDEA_TAB.text: We start on the Idea tab. This is where you describe the web application you want to build. The more detail you provide, the better the AI output will be.

IDEA_TYPING.text: Let's describe a Pomodoro Timer application. We'll include target users, key features, design preferences, and technical requirements using Markdown formatting.

IDEA_SAVED.text: The idea has been saved. It's now stored as a Markdown file that the AI pipeline will read during generation.

MODEL_SETTINGS.text: Below the idea editor, you can configure which AI models to use. There are three model slots: Smart for primary code generation, Fast for quick parsing tasks, and Image for any visual generation.

MODEL_SETTINGS_NOTE.text: The models are loaded from your configured API providers. Make sure to select appropriate models before running the pipeline.

PIPELINE_TAB.text: Now let's move to the Pipeline tab. This is where the AI build process happens.

PIPELINE_OVERVIEW.text: The pipeline diagram shows three stages: Idea input, Build Project, and Complete. The AI reads your description, plans the architecture, and generates all the code in a single step.

PIPELINE_STARTED.text: Let's run the full pipeline. The AI will now read our Pomodoro Timer description and generate a complete, runnable web application.

PIPELINE_RUNNING.text: The pipeline is running. The AI agent is planning the project structure, writing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and creating documentation. This typically takes a few minutes depending on the complexity of the app.

PIPELINE_DONE.text: Excellent! The pipeline has completed successfully. The AI has generated a full Pomodoro Timer application. Let's go see the results.

PIPELINE_SKIPPED.text: We're skipping the pipeline execution for this demo. Let's move on to the results.

RESULTS_TAB.text: The Results tab has multiple sub-tabs for exploring the generated output. Let's start with the live preview.

RESULTS_PREVIEW.text: The Live Preview tab shows an embedded iframe of the generated webapp. Let's refresh it to load the latest version.

RESULTS_PREVIEW_LOADED.text: Here's our generated Pomodoro Timer running live in the preview. You can interact with it directly, and there's a console panel below that captures any JavaScript output or errors.

RESULTS_PREVIEW_SKIPPED.text: Skipping the live preview for now.

RESULTS_FILES.text: The Project Files tab shows all generated files in a browsable file tree. Let's refresh the file list.

RESULTS_FILES_LOADED.text: Here we can see all the files the AI generated — HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and documentation. You can click on any file to view its contents with syntax highlighting.

RESULTS_FILES_SKIPPED.text: Skipping the file browser for now.

RESULTS_README.text: The README tab shows the generated project documentation. The AI creates a comprehensive README explaining the app's features, architecture, and usage instructions.

RESULTS_README_SKIPPED.text: Skipping the README view for now.

RESULTS_DOWNLOAD.text: The Download tab lets you export your generated webapp. You have several options for downloading.

RESULTS_DOWNLOAD_OPTIONS.text: You can download the entire session including all metadata, just the generated code, or a specific subdirectory. The files are packaged as a ZIP archive.

RESULTS_DOWNLOAD_SKIPPED.text: Skipping the download options for now.

UPDATE_TAB.text: Now let's look at the Update tab. This is where you can refine your webapp after the initial build. Instead of starting over, you describe what changes you want and the AI applies them to the existing code.

UPDATE_TYPING.text: Let's write some update notes. We'll request a bug fix, add a couple of new features, and make some design tweaks.

UPDATE_SAVED.text: The update notes are saved. Now let's apply them to the existing project.

UPDATE_STARTED.text: Running the update operation. The AI will read our feedback and modify the generated code accordingly.

UPDATE_RUNNING.text: The update is in progress. The AI is reading our notes and applying targeted changes to the existing codebase rather than regenerating everything from scratch.

UPDATE_DONE.text: The update is complete. The AI has applied our requested changes. Let's check the updated preview.

UPDATE_PREVIEW.text: Here's the updated Pomodoro Timer with our requested changes applied. The iterative refinement workflow lets you converge on exactly what you want through multiple cycles.

UPDATE_SKIPPED.text: We're skipping the update step for this demo.

GIT_TAB.text: The Git tab provides built-in version control for your project. You can track changes, create branches, and manage your webapp's history without leaving the builder.

GIT_INIT.text: We've initialized a Git repository. This lets us track every change the AI makes to our project.

GIT_STATUS.text: The repository status shows all the files that have been created or modified. Let's commit everything.

GIT_COMMITTED.text: Changes committed. Now we have a snapshot of our project that we can always return to.

GIT_LOG.text: The commit history shows all our snapshots. This is especially useful when iterating — you can always go back to a previous version if an update doesn't work out.

GIT_QUICK_ACTIONS.text: There are also quick actions for common workflows like taking a snapshot, starting an experiment branch, or creating a backup ZIP. These combine multiple Git operations into one click.

GIT_SKIPPED.text: Skipping the Git version control section for this demo.

USAGE_TAB.text: Finally, the Usage tab tracks all AI model calls, token counts, and estimated costs for your session.

USAGE_SUMMARY.text: The summary banner shows total prompt tokens, completion tokens, and estimated cost across all operations. Below that, you can see a detailed breakdown by model.

USAGE_TASKS.text: The per-task usage section shows costs for each individual pipeline run or update operation, so you can see exactly where your tokens are being spent.

USAGE_SKIPPED.text: Skipping the usage tracking section for this demo.

LAUNCH_INTRO.text: One last thing — notice the Launch App button in the navigation bar. This opens your generated webapp in a new browser tab, completely standalone.

LAUNCH_READY.text: Your webapp is ready to use. You can share the URL, download the files, or continue iterating with more updates.

OUTRO.text: And that's the complete Webapp Builder workflow! From a plain text description to a fully functional web application — with live preview, iterative refinement, version control, and usage tracking. Describe your idea, let the AI build it, refine it until it's perfect, and ship it. Thank you for watching!
